title: Costco Doesn't Make Its Money Selling Groceries 🛒 #shorts
description:
In fiscal 2026 Costco sold $297.2 billion of goods but made $9.2 billion in profit. Membership fees alone brought in $5.9 billion, about two-thirds of that profit. That's why the $1.50 hot dog combo hasn't changed since 1985.
Source: Costco Wholesale, "Q4 and Fiscal Year 2026 Operating Results" (Sept 24, 2026); Stock Titan / Pulse 2.0 coverage of the same results; Fox Business, "Why Costco hot dogs have kept $1.50 price tag since 1985"; Business Insider. Education, not financial advice.
script: Costco barely makes money selling you groceries. It makes money before you even walk in.
Last year, Costco sold almost three hundred billion dollars of stuff.
But its profit was only about nine point two billion.
Membership fees alone brought in almost six billion. That's about two thirds of the whole profit, from a plastic card.
So Costco can keep prices crazy low. The hot dog combo still costs a dollar fifty, just like in nineteen eighty-five.
Cheap prices make people renew. More than ninety percent of members in the US and Canada come back.
Costco isn't really a store. It's a subscription, with groceries attached.
